blogs.title: Beyond the Classic: Understanding Autoimmune HIT (aHIT)
blogs.description: A deep dive into the emerging phenotype of 'autoimmune HIT' (aHIT). This post explains the pathophysiology of antibodies that activate platelets independently of heparin, why aHIT often presents with more profound thrombocytopenia and a higher risk of thrombosis than classic HIT, and how to recognize this variant in a clinical setting.

blogs.title: The HIT Clock: Why POD 5 Isn't the Only Rule
blogs.description: Clinicians are taught that HIT typically occurs 5-10 days post-exposure, but this case highlights the 'pre-op trap.' We discuss how preoperative heparin exposure (e.g., during cardiac catheterization) can prime the immune system, leading to an unusually early onset of thrombocytopenia that can mislead clinicians into attributing the drop to surgical blood loss or other causes.

blogs.title: Deciphering the SRA: When the 'Gold Standard' is Indeterminate
blogs.description: The Serotonin-Release Assay (SRA) is the gold standard for HIT, but it isn't always straightforward. This post analyzes the aHIT SRA profile—specifically the presence of serotonin release at 0 U/mL of heparin—and explores the significance of partial resistance to Fc receptor blockade, teaching clinicians how to interpret 'indeterminate' lab results in the context of high clinical suspicion.

blogs.title: The Thrombotic Storm: HIT as a Consumptive Coagulopathy
blogs.description: HIT is a paradox: low platelets but high clotting risk. This post examines the systemic hypercoagulability seen in severe aHIT, including the development of arterial strokes, schistocytosis, and falling fibrinogen levels, framing HIT not just as 'low platelets' but as a complex consumptive coagulopathy requiring aggressive anticoagulation.

blogs.title: Managing the Refractory Case: Argatroban, Fondaparinux, and IVIg
blogs.description: When standard DTI therapy isn't enough, what's next? This post discusses the management tensions in severe aHIT, comparing the use of Argatroban versus Fondaparinux and the role of high-dose intravenous immunoglobulin (IVIg) as a rescue therapy to stabilize platelet counts in the setting of profound thrombocytopenia.
